title: spec: retire tombstones, conversions and migration entries older than one protocol major; a strict unknown-key refusal with an upgrade-guide link takes over (maintainer ruling D2 = A)
body:
> **Premise checked before dispatch** (domain:spec seat 2, 2026-10-26): readings and corrections in comment 6409932697 (https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/25767#issuecomment-6409932697). The goal below is unchanged.

Filing-gate category: ③ maintainer-directed. Tesla ruled the whole-project assessment's D2 on 2026-10-25 09:23Z in the director thread, answering the option list (A = keep one major, then a strict unknown-key error plus an upgrade-guide link; tombstones and migration entries deleted together; B = two majors; C = keep forever, as today): 「D4 · 固定发版日 没必要；其他同意 ，npm dist-tag 手工清理 应该立一张管理者维护的卡」 — "其他同意" covers D2 = A. ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route. Spec seat 1 is paused, so nobody dispatches this until triage has touched it.

Governing text: ADR-0087 (`docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`) — D3 keeps every conversion "forever" for `migrate meta --from N` above the support floor (lines ~143–190, ~380–390, ~551). This ruling changes that permanence, so the PR carries an ADR-0087 amendment (Tier H, human merge).

## The rule, as ruled

- A retirement (a `retiredKey()` tombstone, its `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` / `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` entry, its `semantic/` migration entry, and the matching conversion in `conversions/registry.ts`) lives for **one protocol major after the one it was retired in**. At protocol 18 that keeps the 17.x and 18.x retirements and removes everything retired in 16.x or earlier.
- After removal the key is refused by the strict schema as an unknown key — still a loud refusal — and that refusal names the upgrade guide (link) instead of a per-key tombstone sentence.
- The support floor for `os migrate meta --from N` rises to match (16 and below: refusal + link only, no conversion). The releases page says so.
- The next major repeats the same cut; no gate is added for it (new gates default to no; Tesla named none).

## Readings (main `5874d25`, 2026-10-25)

- `conversions/registry.ts`: 18,337 lines; `retiredAfter` distribution 15.0.0 ×5, 16.1.0 ×45, 17.x ×96, 18.x ×4 — so 50 conversions are in scope for this cut.
  Re-check: `grep -n "retiredAfter" packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts | grep -oE "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | sort | uniq -c`
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/`: retired-keys 17 ×29 / 18 ×250; retired-defs 17 ×53 / 18 ×173; semantic 17 ×77 / 18 ×418 — no 16.x entry files remain, so the 16.x population is the tombstones and conversions themselves.
  Re-check: `for d in retired-keys retired-defs semantic; do ls packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/$d | cut -d. -f1 | sort | uniq -c; done`
- `retiredKey(` call sites in `packages/spec/src`: 936. Which of them are 16.x retirements is not measured here; the dev derives the population from the ledger/conversions and lists it in the PR, ⛔ never by guessing from guidance prose.

## Business rationale

- Who pays today: the fleet. In the assessment's two-week window 133 of 387 commits touching spec touched the retirement machinery (~55k lines of conversions and migrations), and 72 conversions were kept past their `retiredAfter`. Every spec card pays this tax.
- Who loses: an author or AI still writing a key retired in 16.x or earlier gets "unknown key" plus the upgrade-guide link instead of a per-key hint — still a refusal at save/`os validate`, never a silent drop (axis 3 kept).
- Not doing it: the permanent obligation keeps growing with every major.

## Scope for the dev (fork, don't improvise)

1. Enumerate the ≤16.x population (tombstones, ledger rows, conversions, migration entries, generated guide sections) and paste the counts in the PR.
2. Delete them together; make the strict unknown-key refusal carry the upgrade-guide link where it does not already (measure first: name the file that formats the refusal).
3. ADR-0087 amendment + releases-page floor sentence; changeset per AGENTS.md (this changes the load door's accept behaviour for ≤16.x artifacts — report the `Metadata-protocol:` level, likely `narrowed`).
4. Fork back to the card if a 16.x retirement still has a live reader (a test fixture is not a reader; hotcrm / objectui code is).

Reader: the spec seat that claims it after triage (domain:spec), contract-review tier per the skill. Effort guess L (multi-file deletion + ADR).

Duplicate check: semantic searches "retiredKey tombstone lifetime drop migration entries older than one major" (objectstack, 13 hits, all closed and about tombstone wording/placement, none about lifetime) and "D2 retiredKey" (0 open). No open card covers lifetime.

Evidence: whole-project assessment D2, https://claude.ai/artifact/8qxoYjsE4jQC4DJBCF3wm5#D2
